source.title: Soft Prompt Threats: Attacking Safety Alignment and Unlearning in Open-Source LLMs through the Embedding Space
source.authors: Leo Schwinn; David Dobre; Sophie Xhonneux; G. Gidel; Stephan Günnemann

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some figure and table content is garbled in the extracted text, but the relevant results are also stated in prose.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own harmful fine-tuning result, bearing on V1, using a HarmBench attack-success measure. It also tests a different safety-bypass method, embedding-space attacks, which is not one of the versions’ named mechanisms.
record.gate_note: The harmful fine-tuning result is included for V1. Embedding-space attack outcomes are recorded under fits_no_version: they measure harmful compliance, but do not test the listed fine-tuning, first-token KL, compliant-opening, suffix, decoding-change, localization, shallowness-cause, or deepening mechanisms. Results about unlearning and pretraining-data extraction are outside the claim.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes Llama2-7b-chat with QLoRa on 100 harmful Anthropic red-teaming examples and reports held-out HarmBench ASR (88.8%), which bears on V1. Its main method is a continuous adversarial suffix in embedding space, optimised to force an affirmative opening ('Sure, here is...'). That is a suffix attack aimed at getting past the opening, so its ASR results bear on V4 in a white-box continuous form. The study is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that embedding-space attacks bypass safety alignment in open-source models more efficiently than discrete attacks or fine-tuning, including on circuit-breaker models. They add that such attacks recover supposedly unlearned information (Harry Potter Q&A, TOFU) and, in preliminary work, some pretraining data.
record.recipe_differences: The study fine-tunes Llama2 with QLoRa for 50 iterations on 100 filtered Anthropic red-teaming examples and evaluates on held-out HarmBench behaviors. The text does not establish whether this exactly matches the original fine-tuning recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The embedding-space attack’s effectiveness varies by setting: universal attacks on unseen behaviors report different success rates for Llama2-7b-Chat, Mistral-7b-CB, and Llama3-8b-CB; the paper also says the circuit-breaker attacks used 2000 iterations.

fits_no_version.finding: An embedding-attacked Llama2 generated discrete jailbreaks reaching 43.6% ASR on unseen behaviours, versus 0% when not attacked.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Models compromised in embedding space can produce transferable natural-language jailbreaks.

record.problems: The harmful fine-tuning comparison is on one Llama2 model and reports no uncertainty for its 88.8% attack success rate. The paper notes that it did not evaluate whether the affirmative-response objective increases hallucinations, and that correctness of generated responses is not evaluated. Some figure content in the provided extraction is garbled.
record.rows_left_out: No additional directly relevant claim-version outcomes left out. Unlearning and pretraining-data extraction results were omitted because they do not measure the behaviours named in the claim versions.

untested.parts: Only one model and one data size (100 examples, 50 steps) are tested. There is no sweep over example counts and no unattacked baseline ASR is reported.
Prefilling of a compliant response and decoding changes are not tested. Token-level (discrete) suffix results are only in the garbled Fig. 4. No per-position analysis is reported.
Circuit-breaker models are attacked, but no deepening of the kind V7 names (training that spreads safety beyond the first tokens) is evaluated.

missing.what: Per-model ASR and compute time of GCG, AutoDAN, PAIR and adaptive attacks versus embedding attacks, including the low discrete-attack ASR on circuit-breaker models
missing.locator: Fig. 4 (garbled in extraction); §5 Training Data Evaluations

missing.what: Toxicity of fine-tuned Llama2 responses compared with the embedding-attacked and standard Llama2. Fine-tuning raised toxicity less than embedding attacks (Mann-Whitney p=3.5e-21).
Discretising the optimised embedding suffix to the nearest tokens does not give effective attacks
missing.locator: §5 From Continuous to Discrete Threat Models

record.verdict_notes: Linking the embedding attacks to V4 is a judgement call. They are continuous suffixes optimised for an affirmative opening, which matches V4's suffix mechanism, but they are a stronger white-box threat model than token suffixes. The harmful-response ASRs use a HarmBench judge and cumulative best-of-20 scoring, which inflates them relative to one-shot ASR. The authors note that response correctness was not evaluated.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests harmful-data fine-tuning on one Llama2 model, but does not test a range of example counts or establish a general threshold for when refusal is removed.
No per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models is measured.
The study does not test compliant response prefills, adversarial suffixes as specified in the claim, or decoding changes as a bypass of refusal.
No localization of safety behaviour to weights, parameters, or ranks is tested.
The study does not test whether data or a training objective causes safety to be shallow.
No training that deepens safety across response tokens is evaluated.

rows.subject: All models tested for individual embedding attacks
rows.operation_detail: Optimized an individual embedding-space attack on each input and evaluated it on the same data.
rows.note: Aggregate result as reported by the study; the prose says all models, without specifying a model count here. This tests embedding-space attacks, not the mechanisms named in V1–V7.
rows.check: The value is cumulative ASR (success in any of 20 evaluations during optimisation), not one-shot ASR. It covers the six safety models in Fig. 4 (Vicuna, Mistral, Llama2, Llama3, Mistral-CB, Llama3-CB). The attack is an optimised embedding suffix targeting an affirmative opening, so it bears on V4's suffix mechanism.
